fields.statement: Verified at c2db23b07 (attempt 3). go test -trimpath -count=1 ./cmd/rhiza -run 'TestScripts/(repair|describe-golden)$' passes: the repair script reproduces the incident (an uncommitted, index-seen entry overwritten with another entry's bytes; render refuses with 'damaged log'), repair --dry-run names the entry (path and from=index in --json, 'would restore from index' in text) and leaves bytes and mode 644 unchanged, repair restores the original bytes (cmp) at 0444, then render and fold-ok pass; a changed committed entry is restored from HEAD at 0444; an entry the index never saw exits non-zero with 'not restorable' naming it. go test ./internal/index/... passes (TestStoredEntry covers reading stored bytes). The earlier finding is fixed: go test ./internal/api -run TestEveryResponseIsHumaner passes, RepairResponse now has Human(io.Writer). Full ./internal/api tests all PASS; its root-state guard flagged ~/code/.rhiza-root/usage.live.json changing during the 9-minute run, which the live root daemon writes and repair does not touch. Read the diff of internal/api/repair.go: HEAD bytes first, else index bytes only when they decode canonically with the path's change set and ID, written via store.WriteEntryFile, nothing deleted.
